description.narrative:
The goal of the Masimanyane Ibhola Ekhatywaya Ngamantombazana project is to contribute towards the prevention of GBVF and the building of social cohesion by using girl’s soccer to create safe spaces for healthy and purposeful participation.
The purpose of this pilot is to further the whole-of-society approach outlined in National Strategic Plan on GBVF. The aim is to ensure that everyone is involved in addressing GBVF in a systematic, holistic and comprehensive manner.
Project Objectives Through the establishment of a soccer academy in Buffalo City, the objectives of this pilot project are as follows: 1. To make soccer more accessible to young girls as a sport. 2. To challenge and change unhealthy norms and attitudes in young boys who play soccer. 3. To empower young girls to fully participate in an internationally recognised sport. 4. To develop relevant knowledge, skills, and tools that can used to reduce levels of rape, domestic violence and femicide in local communities. 5. To uncover skills that could generate financial income. 6. To create safe spaces for engaging in healthy, purposeful sporting activities.
The Soccer Academy will provide comprehensive training for young aspiring women and men in a safe supportive environment. Our aim is to nurture their skills and promote healing. Additionally, we will ensure that participants have the opportunity to play in soccer matches and fixtures. Furthermore, the Academy will serve as a training center for existing teams, focusing on addressing GBVF issues.
Results Our intention is to achieve the following results in the target sites of implementation: . Visible increase in girls play soccer in public open spaces. . 100% Boys demonstrably understand gender equality on the field, at home and in the community. . 50% Girls are recruited into established national teams. . 10% Annual reduction in GBV incidences across target communities . 5% Annual increase in reporting GBV cases
